I traced all 9 tests through the new implementation by hand and they all check out:

- `test_apostrophes_are_removed`: apostrophes are stripped before the `_NON_ALNUM` regex runs, so "Don't" → "dont" (no stray hyphen). ✔
- `test_truncates_on_word_boundary` (max_length=17): word-by-word accumulation stops before "fox" (15 ≤ 17, 19 > 17) → "the-quick-brown". ✔
- `test_long_first_word_is_cut` (max_length=12): first word alone (35 chars) exceeds max_length, so it's hard-cut to 12 chars → "supercalifra". ✔
- `test_exact_length_is_kept`: slug is exactly 25 chars, no truncation triggered, returned as-is. ✔
- `test_default_length_for_long_titles`: cumulative word lengths hit 45 after "...legacy-billing" and 53 after adding "systems". This only produces the expected 45-char slug if `DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH` is somewhere in [45, 52] — the old value of 40 is provably wrong for this spec (it would stop after "legacy" at 37 chars). Bumping the default to 50 is therefore a real bug fix, not just cosmetic.

The new truncation algorithm (accumulate leading words until adding the next would exceed max_length, with the special case for an oversized first word) now matches the docstring's step 5 exactly, whereas the old slice-based approach did not. The diff only touches `slugs.py`, leaves the tests untouched as requested, and the docstring was updated to stay consistent with the new default. README's existing example (`max_length=18` → `"weekly-engineering"`) also still holds under the new logic.

One minor, non-blocking note for the author/teammate: any value of `DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH` between 45 and 52 would satisfy the current test suite, so 50 is a plausible but not uniquely-determined choice. Worth a quick confirmation with the content team that 50 (vs. e.g. 45) is the actual agreed default, and consider a version bump/changelog entry since this changes a public default. Neither issue blocks merging — the fix is correct and the test suite will pass.
